resolved.title: 切片 Slice
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Slices[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

An array has a fixed size, meaning once defined, you cannot change the number of elements it holds.

To overcome this, Go provides the [b]slice[/b], which is a dynamically-sized view into the elements of an array.

A slice is based on an array and is defined by specifying two indices, a [b]low[/b] and [b]high[/b] bound, separated by a colon:
[code format="go" ]a := [5]int{0, 2, 4, 6, 8}

var s []int = a[1:3]
 [/code]
This code selects the elements with index 1 to 3 from the [b]a[/b] array, including the first given index, but excluding the last.

So, the slice [b]s[/b] will now include the values [2, 4]:[code format="go" codeId="3342"]fmt.Println(s) [/code]
[note]You can omit the low or the high bound. 
Omitting the low bound will take the value 0, while omitting the high bound will take the length of the array.
For example: [b]a[:3][/b] will take the first 3 elements of the array.[/note]

切片是基于数组的，通过指定两个索引，即**低**(low)和**高**(high)边界，并用冒号`:`隔开来定义：

To overcome this, Go provides the slice, which is a dynamically-sized view into the elements of an array.

A slice is based on an array and is defined by specifying two indices, a low and high bound, separated by a colon:

[s0l0!-header][h1]Slices[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

You can access the values of the slice using the same syntax as with arrays:[code format="go" codeId="3343"]a := [5]int{0, 2, 4, 6, 8}
var s []int = a[1:3]
 
fmt.Println(s[1])[/code]
A slice does not store any data; it just describes a section of an underlying array. Changing the elements of a slice modifies the corresponding elements of its underlying array.[code format="go" codeId="3344"]s[0] = 8
fmt.Println(a)[/code]
[note]You can have multiple slices of the same array. A change in any of them will be seen in all slices, as it will affect the underlying array. [/note]

resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Slices[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Go provides a [b]make()[/b] function to create slices. 
This is how you create dynamically-sized arrays. 

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="go" ]a := make([]int, 5) [/code]
The [b]make[/b] function creates an array of the given type and size, and returns a slice that refers to that array.

After creating a slice, we can add append new elements to it using the [b]append[/b]() function:[code format="go" codeId="3345"]a := make([]int, 5)
[b]a = append(a, 8)[/b]
fmt.Println(a) [/code]
The [b]append[/b]() function takes the slice as its first argument and the elements to be added to the end of the slice as its next argument.
It then returns a new slice, containing the old slice plus the new elements appended.
[note]You can append multiple values at once by just comma separating the values as arguments, for example: [b]append(s, 1, 2, 3)[/b][/note]

content.text:
函数**make**创建一个给定类型和大小的数组，并返回一个指向该数组的切片。

在创建一个切片后，可以使用**append**()函数添加新元素：
content.text_html:
The make function creates an array of the given type and size, and returns a slice that refers to that array.

After creating a slice, we can add append new elements to it using the append() function:

函数make创建一个给定类型和大小的数组，并返回一个指向该数组的片断。

在创建一个片断后，我们可以使用append()函数向其添加新元素。

content.content:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
  a := make([]int, 5)
  a = append(a, 8)
  fmt.Println(a)
}

content.text:
`append()`函数将切片作为它的第一个参数，将要添加到切片末尾的元素作为下一个参数。
然后返回一个新的切片，包含旧切片和新添加的元素。
content.text_html:
The append() function takes the slice as its first argument and the elements to be added to the end of the slice as its next argument. It then returns a new slice, containing the old slice plus the new elements appended.

append()函数将片断作为它的第一个参数，将要添加到片断末尾的元素作为它的下一个参数。 然后它返回一个新的片断，包含旧的片断和新添加的元素。

content.text: 你可以一次追加多个值，只需用逗号`,`将这些值作为参数分开，例如：`append(s, 1, 2, 3)`
content.text_html:
You can append multiple values at once by just comma separating the values as arguments, for example: append(s, 1, 2, 3)

请将后续输入的数字存储在一个切片中，并输出切片。
resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Multiple Inputs[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The [b]make[/b]() function allows you to make dynamically sized arrays, which can use the [b]append[/b]() function to add new elements to it.
This is useful when, for example, you need to take multiple inputs and store them in an array.

Your program needs to take a number, indicating the number of inputs, followed by those inputs. The input numbers should be stored in an array and be outputted as the result of the program.

[b]Sample Input:[/b]
3
42
88
11
 
[b]Sample Output:[/b]
[42 88 11]

[note]The first number indicates that there are going to be [b]3[/b] numbers as input.[/note]
